Reproducing Chen et al. (2017) from dandiset 000015¶

Paper. Chen T-W, Li N, Daie K, Svoboda K (2017). A map of anticipatory activity in mouse motor cortex. Neuron 94, 866-879. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2017.05.005. The claims file (claims/000015/10.1016-j.neuron.2017.05.005.yaml) was written from the version of record, main text, figure legends and STAR Methods; the Supplemental Information was not in the text read.

Dataset. DANDI:000015, version 0.220126.1914 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000015/0.220126.1914). The paper cites no DANDI version: it names a CRCNS deposit (10.6080/K0S180F9), and that DOI resolves to a placeholder record ("CRCNS.org ssc-8TBD", "This data is not yet available"). This is the only published version of the dandiset; the draft has the same 210 assets and size, so the published version is pinned. The files are streamed; nothing is downloaded.

Outside data. The paper compares its imaging with tagged PT and IT units from Li et al. (2015). Those units are on DANDI:000010, version 0.220126.1905, which is used for the link claim and for ephys-pt-it-onset-not-detected below (spike times, trial tables, behavioural events and laser power of the sessions with tagged units).

Questions. Five questions were asked of a reader (questions/000015.yaml) and answered. The paper settles none of them; each answer wrote readings into the claims file, and every claim they touch is run under them here: dF/F with a baseline F0 at or below zero (reading V1, the Methods' formula, decides; V2, without the ROIs concerned, is reported), the onset rule (S1, the first bin over threshold, and S2, the first bin from which it stays over threshold to the go cue), the sample-epoch level and end of delay of figs4-peak-shift (L1, L2, E1, E2), the delay value of fig6-lick-direction-spread (mean and maximum), and the method for the Li et al. (2015) units. A sixth question, asked after the first verification and not yet answered, is over what window the peak of figs4-peak-shift is taken; the whole extracted window is used, and the peak before the go cue is shown.

What the dandiset holds. Two-photon imaging of 105 image planes (each deposited twice) from six mice, with the trial table, the sample, delay and go times, ROI traces and neuropil traces, an ROI table with PT, IT or unknown labels, and an area label (left ALM or left vM1, the paper's MM) per plane. It holds no plane depth, no stereotactic coordinates, no lick times, no whisker video, no wide-field imaging, no silicon probe recordings and no photoinhibition data.

The conventions T, M, A, D, B and O cited below are those of the claims file's opening comment; the helper module chen2017.py says where each parameter comes from.

import collections
import re
import time
import warnings

import h5py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import chen2017 as C

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
assets = C.list_assets()
headers = C.read_headers(assets)
print(f"read {len(headers)} files of dandiset {C.DANDISET_ID} version {C.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

# Copies of one plane share subject, session, frame and ROI counts, trial table and the first and
# last 200 frames of both trace series; each plane is counted once, as its first path.
groups = collections.defaultdict(list)
for h in headers:
    groups[C.content_key(h)].append(h)
planes = sorted((sorted(v, key=lambda h: h["path"])[0] for v in groups.values()), key=lambda h: h["path"])
results = C.process_planes(planes, shuffle_seed=0, start_events=("sample", "start_time"))
print(f"processed {len(planes)} planes in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

# One row per ROI.
cells = pd.DataFrame({
    "plane": np.concatenate([[i] * h["n_rois"] for i, h in enumerate(planes)]),
    "animal": np.concatenate([[h["subject"]] * h["n_rois"] for h in planes]),
    "area": np.concatenate([[h["area"]] * h["n_rois"] for h in planes]),
    "cell_type": np.concatenate([h["cell_type"] for h in planes]),
    "included": np.concatenate([h["included"] for h in planes]),
    "f0_min": np.concatenate([r["T1"]["f0_min"] for r in results]),
    "f0_nonpositive": np.concatenate([r["T1"]["f0_nonpositive"] for r in results]),
    "dff_abs_max": np.concatenate([r["T1"]["dff_abs_max"] for r in results]),
})
area, ctype = cells.area.values, cells.cell_type.values
animal, plane = cells.animal.values, cells.plane.values
ALM, MM = area == "ALM", area == "MM"
A = {b: C.assemble(planes, results, b) for b in ("T1", "T2")}

processed 105 planes in 488 s

Every plane is deposited twice: 105 pairs of files with the same size, the same trial table and the same first and last 200 frames of both trace series, but different identifiers (for example an041_2014-08-23_21 and an041_2014-08-23_43) and different digests. Three pairs read in full (above) have every dataset identical except identifier and file_create_date; the other pairs are compared only on the parts listed. Each plane is counted once. ImagingPlane.location is "ALM" in every file, also in the 47 planes whose experiment_description says "left_vm1"; the area used here (convention A, reading A1) is from experiment_description, and its counts are checked against the paper's below. The frame rates (13.95 and 14.20 Hz) agree with the stated 14 Hz. The traces are in "a.u.".

The trial table holds 'hit', 'miss', 'ignore' and 'non-performing' outcomes. Every early-lick trial has outcome and instruction 'non-performing', so its pole position is not recorded; 'ignore' trials (no lick after the go cue) are left out as convention T says. On every analysed trial the go cue comes 4.2 s after the sample event and the delay starts 1.2 s after it, as the paper's sample (1.2 s) and delay (3 s) epochs require, while the trial table's start_time is 0.623 s before sample. So the paper's trial start, at which the claims file puts the go cue 4.2 s earlier, is the sample event, and it is used as trial start throughout. The traces cover the trial table to within a frame. A few analysed trials whose window runs past the end of the recording are dropped (count above).

The ROI counts are those of the paper (checked under neuron-counts). PT and IT labels are present in three mice (an063, an064, an066), as the paper says for its retrograde labelling. The included column marks 8,655 of 15,431 ROIs, but the paper's counts use all ROIs and nothing says what excluded the others; all ROIs are used here, and the included ROIs are shown as a variant where the counts matter. The files hold no plane depth: the ImagingPlane has no depth, origin or coordinates field, and no text value of any plane names a depth, a coordinate or a layer (the search above; the only matches are the area names). The behavioural events are sample, delay and go in every plane, so there are no lick times. There are no whisker data and no other recordings, so the claims that need these are blocked.

After neuropil subtraction (r = 0.7) the baseline F0 is small, and for 0.26% of ROI-trials it is zero or negative, in 1,262 ROIs. dF/F = (F - F0)/F0 then reaches thousands. The paper does not say how such trials are treated (question answered): the claims file's reading V1, dF/F as computed by the Methods' formula, decides, and V2, the ROIs with F0 <= 0 on any trial left out, is reported as a check in the claims that cite it.

Clock check. The ROI traces and the trial table share one clock if trial-type selectivity appears only after the task events that cause it. Below, per bin, the fraction of ROIs with a significant object-location (alpha) or lick-direction (beta) factor, with the true trial types, with the trial types permuted within each plane (the null), and with the trials aligned to the trial table's start_time in place of sample.

In [6]:
g = A["T1"]["times"]
E = A["T1"]["epochs"]
sig_true = A["T1"]["sig"]
sig_shuf = A["T1"]["shuffled"]["sig"]
p_start = np.concatenate([r["T1_start_time"]["p"] for r in results])
sig_start = p_start < C.ALPHA
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.2), sharey=True)
for k, name in enumerate(["object location (alpha)", "lick direction (beta)"]):
    ax = axes[k]
    for s, lab in ((sig_true, "trial types, aligned to sample"), (sig_shuf, "permuted trial types"),
                   (sig_start, "aligned to start_time")):
        ax.plot(g, s[..., k].mean(0), label=lab)
    for x in (0, 1.2, 4.2):
        ax.axvline(x, color="k", lw=0.5)
    ax.set_title(name); ax.set_xlabel("time from trial start (s)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction of ROIs, p < 0.01"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
for k, name in enumerate(["alpha", "beta"]):
    ft, fs, fa = sig_true[..., k].mean(0), sig_shuf[..., k].mean(0), sig_start[..., k].mean(0)
    print(f"{name}: true, before trial start {ft[E['pre']].mean():.4f}; max {ft.max():.4f} at {g[ft.argmax()]:.2f} s | "
          f"permuted, range {fs.min():.4f} to {fs.max():.4f} | aligned to start_time, max {fa.max():.4f} at {g[fa.argmax()]:.2f} s")
first_a = g[np.flatnonzero(sig_true[..., 0].mean(0) > 0.02)[0]]
first_a_start = g[np.flatnonzero(sig_start[..., 0].mean(0) > 0.02)[0]]
print(f"First bin where alpha-significant ROIs exceed 2%: {first_a:.2f} s aligned to sample, "
      f"{first_a_start:.2f} s aligned to start_time (difference {first_a_start - first_a:.2f} s)")

alpha: true, before trial start 0.0106; max 0.0426 at 1.58 s | permuted, range 0.0085 to 0.0127 | aligned to start_time, max 0.0418 at 2.22 s
beta: true, before trial start 0.0105; max 0.0710 at 4.87 s | permuted, range 0.0085 to 0.0137 | aligned to start_time, max 0.0684 at 5.52 s
First bin where alpha-significant ROIs exceed 2%: 0.65 s aligned to sample, 1.29 s aligned to start_time (difference 0.65 s)

Before trial start the fraction of ROIs with a significant factor is at the 1% the test allows, and with permuted trial types it stays near 1% in every bin. With the true trial types, object-location selectivity rises after the pole starts to move and lick-direction selectivity after the go cue; aligned to start_time the same rise comes later on the time axis, as the offset between the two events predicts (0.65 s for the first bin above 2%, against the 0.623 s offset, within a frame). The traces and the trial table are consistent with one clock; the check shows the alignment to within a few frames, not exactly.

The silicon probe recordings, wide-field imaging, photoinhibition and whisker data are therefore not public there. A search of DANDI by the paper's DOI and by its authors finds only this dandiset. Other archives were not searched here.

early-lick-fraction¶

Mice licked early, during the delay epoch, on 13.3% +- 10% of trials, and these trials were not analysed. (Expected 13.3, tolerance 10, percent.)

In [8]:
rows = []
for h in planes:
    n = len(h["outcome"])
    rows.append({"subject": h["subject"], "session": h["session"], "n": n, "early": int(h["early_lick"].sum()),
                 "with_lick": n - int((h["outcome"] == "ignore").sum())})
el = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out = []
for den in ("n", "with_lick"):
    per_plane = 100 * el.early / el[den]
    ses = el.groupby(["subject", "session"])[["early", den]].sum()
    mouse = el.groupby("subject")[["early", den]].sum()
    out += [
        {"reading": "(a) mean over planes", "denominator": den, "mean": per_plane.mean(), "sd": per_plane.std()},
        {"reading": "(b) mean over sessions", "denominator": den, "mean": (100 * ses.early / ses[den]).mean(), "sd": (100 * ses.early / ses[den]).std()},
        {"reading": "(c) mean over mice", "denominator": den, "mean": (100 * mouse.early / mouse[den]).mean(), "sd": (100 * mouse.early / mouse[den]).std()},
        {"reading": "(d) pooled", "denominator": den, "mean": 100 * el.early.sum() / el[den].sum(), "sd": np.nan}]
res = pd.DataFrame(out)
res["within_13.3_pm_10"] = (res["mean"] - 13.3).abs() <= 10
print(res.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPer mouse (percent of all trials):", (100 * el.groupby("subject").early.sum() / el.groupby("subject").n.sum()).round(1).to_dict())

imaging-sample¶

fraction-selective-alm-mm¶

A large fraction of neurons distinguished between trial types, 23% in MM (1,523 of 6,594) and 31% in ALM (2,754 of 8,837).

Readings from the criterion: rule R1 (one significant bin) or R2 (two consecutive), window W1 (4.6 s before to 2.5 s after the go cue), W2 (the whole extracted window) or W3 (trial start to 2.5 s after the go cue), bins T1 or T2, area A1.

In [12]:
def selective_neurons(anysel, times, rule, window):
    w = {"W1": (times >= -0.4 - 1e-9) & (times <= 6.7 + 1e-9), "W2": np.ones(len(times), bool),
         "W3": (times >= 0) & (times <= 6.7 + 1e-9)}[window]
    a = anysel[:, w]
    return a.any(1) if rule == "R1" else (a[:, 1:] & a[:, :-1]).any(1)

rows = []
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    for rule in ("R1", "R2"):
        for win in ("W1", "W2", "W3"):
            s = selective_neurons(A[b]["any"], A[b]["times"], rule, win)
            r = {"bins": b, "rule": rule, "window": win, "ALM_n": int(s[ALM].sum()), "ALM_%": 100 * s[ALM].mean(),
                 "MM_n": int(s[MM].sum()), "MM_%": 100 * s[MM].mean()}
            r["all_within"] = (abs(r["MM_n"] - 1523) <= 152 and abs(r["ALM_n"] - 2754) <= 275 and
                               abs(r["MM_%"] - 23) <= 2.3 and abs(r["ALM_%"] - 31) <= 3.1)
            r["ALM_higher"] = r["ALM_%"] > r["MM_%"]
            v2 = cells.f0_min.values > 0
            r["V2_ALM_n"], r["V2_ALM_%"] = int(s[ALM & v2].sum()), 100 * s[ALM & v2].mean()
            r["V2_MM_n"], r["V2_MM_%"] = int(s[MM & v2].sum()), 100 * s[MM & v2].mean()
            if b == "T1":
                sn = selective_neurons(A[b]["shuffled"]["any"], A[b]["times"], rule, win)
                r["null_ALM_%"], r["null_MM_%"] = 100 * sn[ALM].mean(), 100 * sn[MM].mean()
            rows.append(r)
fs = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(fs.round(1).to_string(index=False))
print("\nReadings with all four values within tolerance (V1, deciding):", int(fs.all_within.sum()))
print("V2 (ROIs with F0 <= 0 on any trial left out, a check):", int((ALM & v2).sum()), "ALM and", int((MM & v2).sum()), "MM ROIs remain")

Result: not reproduced. No reading puts all four values within tolerance under V1, the reading that decides. Rule R1 marks 78% to 91% of ROIs as selective, and 72% to 85% with permuted trial types, so it counts chance bins. Rule R2 (permuted: 10.5% to 14.3%) with T1 bins comes closest: ALM 2,853 (32.3%) and MM 1,736 (26.3%) in window W3, and ALM 2,877 (32.6%) and MM 1,755 (26.6%) in window W1; ALM is within tolerance, MM is above it (at most 1,675 and 25.3%). With T2 bins R2 gives 45% and 38% (W1). ALM has the higher fraction under every reading. Under V2 (a check, 8,315 ALM and 5,854 MM ROIs) R2 with T1 bins gives ALM 2,762 (33.2%) and MM 1,656 (28.3%) in W3, and ALM 2,786 (33.5%) and MM 1,675 (28.6%) in W1, still above the tolerance on the MM fraction under every reading.

figs5-single-coefficient¶

The selectivity of most neurons can be attributed to one of the three coefficients, especially early in the trial, so most neurons mainly encode one behavioural variable at a time.

      f"selective ROIs per bin {sh['any'].sum(0)[w].min()} to {sh['any'].sum(0)[w].max()}")

T1: bins from trial start to the go cue 59, with pure fraction > 0.5: 59; range 0.845 to 0.928; selective ROIs per bin 413 to 985; after the go cue mean 0.793 (min 0.720)

T2: bins from trial start to the go cue 63, with pure fraction > 0.5: 63; range 0.826 to 0.923; selective ROIs per bin 403 to 1108; after the go cue mean 0.784 (min 0.716)
T1 with permuted trial types (null): pure / selective from trial start to the go cue 0.845 to 0.911 (mean 0.876), bins above 0.5: 59 of 59; selective ROIs per bin 368 to 445

Result: reproduced. In every bin from trial start to the go cue, more than half of the selective ROIs are purely selective (lowest 0.845 with T1 bins, 0.826 with T2). After the go cue the fraction is 0.793 (T1) on average. With permuted trial types the same fraction is 0.845 to 0.911 and above one half in all 59 bins, so the criterion is met by chance-level selectivity too: the measure does not tell the result from chance, and the outcome rests on the criterion alone.

fig4a-lick-direction-epochs¶

Different neurons coded for lick direction in different epochs, some during the sample and delay epochs before licking, some during the response epoch, and some after the mouse stopped consuming water.

In [14]:
def fig4a_counts(pure, t):
    pb = pure[..., 1]
    first = np.where(pb.any(1), np.argmax(pb, 1), -1)
    go_bin = np.flatnonzero(t >= C.GO)[0]
    return {"delay": int(pb[:, (t >= C.SAMPLE_END) & (t < C.GO)].any(1).sum()),
            "first_after_go": int((first >= go_bin).sum()),
            "after_go_plus_2s": int(pb[:, t > C.GO + 2].any(1).sum())}
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    print(b, fig4a_counts(A[b]["pure"], A[b]["times"]))
print("T1 with permuted trial types (null):", fig4a_counts(A["T1"]["shuffled"]["pure"], A["T1"]["times"]))
print("Lick times are not in the files, so the median last lick cannot be computed.")

T1 {'delay': 4125, 'first_after_go': 3611, 'after_go_plus_2s': 4426}
T2 {'delay': 3825, 'first_after_go': 3514, 'after_go_plus_2s': 4155}
T1 with permuted trial types (null): {'delay': 3273, 'first_after_go': 2526, 'after_go_plus_2s': 3196}
Lick times are not in the files, so the median last lick cannot be computed.

Result: reproduced. With T1 bins, 4,125 ROIs are purely lick-direction selective in the delay epoch, 3,611 are first so after the go cue, and 4,426 more than 2 s after the go cue (T2: 3,825, 3,514 and 4,155). With permuted trial types the same counts are 3,273, 2,526 and 3,196, so each group exceeds chance, but most of each count is what chance bins alone give; the criterion asks only that such ROIs exist, which the permuted labels also satisfy. The time after the last lick cannot be tested: lick times are not in the files.

fig4b-object-location-memory¶

Many object-location-selective neurons were selective during the sample epoch, and a subset coded object location mainly in the delay epoch after the pole was removed, some up to the end of the delay.

In [15]:
def fig4b_counts(pure, t):
    pa = pure[..., 0]
    d = pa[:, (t >= C.SAMPLE_END) & (t < C.GO)].sum(1); tot = pa.sum(1)
    return {"sample": int(pa[:, (t >= 0) & (t < C.SAMPLE_END)].any(1).sum()),
            "most_bins_in_delay": int(((tot > 0) & (d > tot / 2)).sum()),
            "last_0.5s_before_go": int(pa[:, (t >= C.GO - 0.5) & (t < C.GO)].any(1).sum())}
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    print(b, fig4b_counts(A[b]["pure"], A[b]["times"]))
print("T1 with permuted trial types (null):", fig4b_counts(A["T1"]["shuffled"]["pure"], A["T1"]["times"]))

T1 {'sample': 2148, 'most_bins_in_delay': 2487, 'last_0.5s_before_go': 1149}
T2 {'sample': 2067, 'most_bins_in_delay': 2483, 'last_0.5s_before_go': 1074}
T1 with permuted trial types (null): {'sample': 1694, 'most_bins_in_delay': 1719, 'last_0.5s_before_go': 707}

Result: reproduced. With T1 bins, 2,148 ROIs are purely object-location selective in the sample epoch, 2,487 have most of their object-location bins in the delay, and 1,149 are selective in the last 0.5 s before the go cue (T2: 2,067, 2,483, 1,074). With permuted trial types the counts are 1,694, 1,719 and 707, so each group exceeds chance; the criterion asks only that such ROIs exist, which the permuted labels also satisfy.

fig4c-outcome-after-lick¶

Outcome-selective neurons typically became selective after the answer lick; some preferred correct and others error trials, and some kept the outcome long after the trial ended.

In [16]:
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    t = A[b]["times"]; pg = A[b]["pure"][..., 2]; K = A[b]["coef"][..., 2]
    ever = pg.any(1); first = np.argmax(pg, 1); go_bin = np.flatnonzero(t >= C.GO)[0]
    after = ever & (first >= go_bin)
    sign_first = np.sign(K[np.arange(len(K)), first])[ever]
    print(f"{b}: purely outcome-selective ROIs {ever.sum()}, first bin after the go cue {after.sum()} "
          f"({after.sum() / ever.sum():.3f}); gamma sign at the first bin: correct-preferring {(sign_first > 0).sum()}, "
          f"error-preferring {(sign_first < 0).sum()}; latest outcome-selective bin {t[np.flatnonzero(pg.any(0))[-1]]:.2f} s")
    if b == "T1":
        s2 = (pg[:, 1:] & pg[:, :-1])
        ever2 = s2.any(1); first2 = np.argmax(s2, 1)
        print(f"   variant, two consecutive bins (as rule R2): {ever2.sum()} ROIs, first after the go cue "
              f"{(ever2 & (first2 >= go_bin)).sum() / ever2.sum():.3f}")
pgs = A["T1"]["shuffled"]["pure"][..., 2]
evs = pgs.any(1)
print(f"T1 permuted (null): {evs.sum()} ROIs, first after the go cue {(evs & (np.argmax(pgs, 1) >= go_bin)).sum() / evs.sum():.3f}")

T1: purely outcome-selective ROIs 9431, first bin after the go cue 3892 (0.413); gamma sign at the first bin: correct-preferring 4157, error-preferring 5274; latest outcome-selective bin 9.17 s
   variant, two consecutive bins (as rule R2): 1463 ROIs, first after the go cue 0.785
T2: purely outcome-selective ROIs 8892, first bin after the go cue 3715 (0.418); gamma sign at the first bin: correct-preferring 3974, error-preferring 4918; latest outcome-selective bin 9.14 s
T1 permuted (null): 8070 ROIs, first after the go cue 0.296

Result: not reproduced. Of the ROIs purely outcome selective in any bin (9,431 with T1 bins), 41.3% have their first such bin after the go cue (T2 41.8%), below the half the criterion requires. Most of these ROIs have only chance bins: with permuted trial types 8,070 ROIs qualify, 29.6% of them first after the go cue. Requiring two consecutive bins (a variant, not deciding) leaves 1,463 ROIs, 78.5% of them first after the go cue. Both signs of gamma occur (4,157 correct-preferring and 5,274 error-preferring at the first bin), and outcome selectivity lasts to the end of the window (9.17 s after trial start).

fig5-mixed-response-epoch¶

Most neurons with mixed selectivity were seen during the response epoch; a subset responded in only one trial type and a few switched the variable they coded during the trial.

        print(f"  {b} {name}: {out}")

Result: not reproduced. The mean dF/F of MM ROIs peaks after that of ALM (6.09 against 4.52 s with T1 bins, 6.14 against 4.54 s with T2), so the MM mean does not peak earlier, and none of the 8 combinations of bins and readings L1, L2, E1, E2 is reproduced under V1. The other part holds under all of them: the ALM mean at the end of the delay (0.212 in the last bin, 0.205 over the last 0.5 s, T1) is above its sample-epoch mean (0.112) and maximum (0.137). Under V2, without the ROIs with F0 <= 0, which dominate the MM mean, MM peaks at 4.80 s, still after ALM (4.52 s). The peak is taken over the whole extracted window, the bins of convention T. Searching only before the go cue (a variant, not deciding), MM peaks before ALM under every bin and dF/F reading: V1 2.08 against 4.16 s (T1) and 0.80 against 4.14 s (T2), V2 1.51 against 4.09 s (T1) and 1.53 against 4.14 s (T2); within the delay epoch alone V1 gives 2.08 against 4.16 s (T1) and 2.60 against 4.14 s (T2). So the outcome turns on the window of the peak, which the criterion does not name; a question has been asked, and the outcome is kept on the whole window until it is answered.

fig8d-pt-earlier-than-it¶

In ALM, lick direction selectivity (|beta|) was stronger and earlier in PT than in IT neurons, with an onset difference of 1.4 +- 0.6 s (p < 0.01, bootstrap).

Reading I1 (deep ALM IT) needs depth and cannot be run; reading I2 (all ALM IT) is run with bins T1 and T2, baselines O1 and O2, onset rules S1 (first bin over the threshold) and S2 (first bin from which the curve stays over it up to the go cue), and bootstraps H1 (hierarchical) and H2 (over cells). The threshold is the baseline mean plus 6 baseline SD, and each resample finds its onsets again by the same rule.

In [25]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(82)
pt, it = ALM & (ctype == "PT"), ALM & (ctype == "IT")
rows = []
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    t = A[b]["times"]; ab = np.abs(A[b]["coef_sig"][..., 1])
    cp, ci = ab[pt].mean(0), ab[it].mean(0)
    for hier in (True, False):
        # One set of resamples per bootstrap; every baseline and rule finds its onset again in each.
        d = {(o, r): [] for o in ("O1", "O2") for r in ("S1", "S2")}
        for _ in range(1000):
            ip, ii = C.joint_resample(animal, plane, [pt, it], rng, hier)
            bp, bi = ab[ip].mean(0), ab[ii].mean(0)
            for (o, r), lst in d.items():
                lst.append(C.onset(bi, t, o, rule=r) - C.onset(bp, t, o, rule=r))
        for (o, r), lst in d.items():
            dd = np.array(lst)
            on_p, on_i = C.onset(cp, t, o, rule=r), C.onset(ci, t, o, rule=r)
            rows.append({"bins": b, "baseline": o, "rule": r, "bootstrap": "H1" if hier else "H2",
                         "PT_onset": on_p, "IT_onset": on_i, "IT_minus_PT": on_i - on_p,
                         "boot_sd": np.nanstd(dd), "p_not_earlier": np.mean(~(dd > 0)), "no_onset": int(np.isnan(dd).sum()),
                         "PT_max": cp.max(), "IT_max": ci.max()})
res = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["bins", "rule", "baseline", "bootstrap"])
res["within_1.4_pm_0.6"] = (res.IT_minus_PT - 1.4).abs() <= 0.6
res["p_below_0.01"] = res.p_not_earlier < 0.01
print(res.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nCombinations within 1.4 +- 0.6 s:", int(res["within_1.4_pm_0.6"].sum()), "; with p < 0.01:", int(res["p_below_0.01"].sum()),
      "; both:", int((res["within_1.4_pm_0.6"] & res["p_below_0.01"]).sum()), "of", len(res))

for x in (0, 1.2, 4.2):
    plt.axvline(x, color="k", lw=0.5)
plt.xlabel("time from trial start (s)"); plt.ylabel("mean |beta|"); plt.legend(); plt.show()

Result: reproduced. Mean |beta| is larger in ALM PT than in ALM IT ROIs (maximum 0.229 against 0.084, T1; 0.231 against 0.085, T2). With onset rule S2, T2 bins and the bootstrap over cells (H2), the IT onset follows the PT onset by 1.80 s (baseline O1, bootstrap SD 0.42 s, p = 0.003) and 1.40 s (O2, SD 0.43 s, p = 0.006), within 1.4 +- 0.6 s at p < 0.01, as the criterion requires under one combination. The result is not robust across readings: rule S2 puts the difference within tolerance in all 8 of its combinations (1.29 to 1.80 s), but with T1 bins p is 0.021 (O2) and 0.170 (O1) under H2, and 0.065 to 0.319 with the hierarchical bootstrap (H1); rule S1, the first single bin, gives 0.20 to 0.22 s, or -1.08 s (T1, O2), with p from 0.31 to 0.52. With S2 and H1 many resamples have no onset (up to 307 of 1,000, counted as PT not earlier). Per mouse (T1, O1, S1) PT is earlier in an063 and an064 and later in an066. Reading I1 (deep IT only) could not be run. The passing combinations use T2 bins of 66.7 ms interpolated from frames of 71.7 ms (13.95 Hz) or 70.4 ms (14.20 Hz), so neighbouring T2 bins are correlated and the onset is not sharper than a frame.

fig8d-error-outnumber-correct¶

Overall, neurons preferring error trials outnumbered those preferring correct trials.

In [27]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(84)
for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    t = A[b]["times"]; w = (t >= C.GO) & (t <= C.GO + 2.5 + 1e-9)
    pg = A[b]["pure"][:, w, 2]; P = A[b]["p"][:, w, 2]; K = A[b]["coef"][:, w, 2]
    best = np.where(pg, P, 2).argmin(1)
    sgn_all = np.sign(K[np.arange(len(K)), best])
    v = A[b]["coef_sig"][:, w, 2].mean(1)
    for name, keep in (("V1, all ROIs", np.ones(len(cells), bool)), ("V2, F0 > 0 on every trial", cells.f0_min.values > 0)):
        has = pg.any(1) & keep
        sgn = sgn_all[has]
        n_err, n_cor = int((sgn < 0).sum()), int((sgn > 0).sum())
        bt = stats.binomtest(n_err, n_err + n_cor, 0.5)
        boot = np.array([v[C.joint_resample(animal, plane, [keep], rng)[0]].mean() for _ in range(1000)])
        m = v[keep].mean()
        print(f"{b} {name}: (a) error-preferring {n_err}, correct-preferring {n_cor}, binomial p = {bt.pvalue:.2e}; "
              f"(b) mean gamma {m:.4f}, bootstrap SD {boot.std():.4f}, ratio {m / boot.std():.2f}, below -2 SD: {m < -2 * boot.std()}")

v = A["T1"]["coef_sig"][:, w, 2].mean(1)
print("by animal (T1), mean gamma: " + "; ".join(f"{a} {v[animal == a].mean():.4f}" for a in np.unique(animal)))

Result: not reproduced. Under V1, the reading that decides, reading (a) finds error preference: among ROIs purely outcome selective after the go cue, 2,825 prefer error trials and 2,004 correct trials (T1, binomial p = 2.8e-32), and T2 agrees (2,730 against 1,933). Reading (b) does not reach its bound: the mean gamma over all ROIs is negative (-0.0082, T1), and in every mouse, but 1.81 bootstrap SDs from zero (T2 1.70). The criterion requires both readings and names no partial outcome, so the claim is not reproduced, as for the other bootstrap claims whose direction holds but whose bound does not. Under V2, a check, (a) holds (2,722 against 1,927) and (b) reaches 2.20 SD with T1 bins, past the bound, and 2.00 SD with T2, which the printed test puts just short of it.

fig8d-mm-object-location (blocked; a part without depth)¶

MM neurons showed strong object location selectivity in superficial and deep layers and in PT and IT cells, PT cells particularly in the early delay; neither PT nor IT neurons in MM showed prominent lick direction selectivity before licking.

The criterion's groups are split by depth (deep PT, deep IT, deep other, superficial IT, superficial other), and the files hold no depth, so the claim is blocked. PT neurons are deep by the paper's account (fig8c-pt-deep-only, whose depth part is itself untested), so the PT group of part (a), MM PT against ALM PT, is the one comparison that needs no depth in the files; it rests on that assumption and does not decide. The same comparisons for IT and other ROIs of the three labelled mice, without the depth split, and the quantities of parts (b) and (c) without depth, are printed for reference.

In [28]:

            mm_, al_ = aa[gm][:, w].mean(0).max(), aa[ga][:, w].mean(0).max()
            extra = ""

                bm, ba = [], []
                for _ in range(1000):
                    im, ia = C.joint_resample(animal, plane, [gm, ga], rng)
                    bm.append(aa[im][:, w].mean(0).max() if len(im) else np.nan)
                    ba.append(aa[ia][:, w].mean(0).max() if len(ia) else np.nan)
                bm, ba = np.array(bm), np.array(ba)
                both = np.isfinite(bm) & np.isfinite(ba)
                extra = (f"; bootstrap SD {np.nanstd(bm):.4f} (MM) and {np.nanstd(ba):.4f} (ALM), resamples without MM or "
                         f"ALM cells {int((~both).sum())}, MM above ALM in {np.mean(bm[both] > ba[both]):.3f} of the others")
            print(f"   {p_}{' (part a for PT, assuming PT deep)' if p_ == 'PT' else ' (no depth split, reference)'}: "
                  f"MM n={gm.sum()} max {mm_:.4f}, ALM n={ga.sum()} max {al_:.4f}, MM larger: {mm_ > al_}{extra}")
        first_delay = {p_: aa[MM & lab_m & (proj == p_) & keep][:, ed].mean() for p_ in ("PT", "IT", "other")}
        print("   (b) reference, mean |alpha| over the first second of the delay in MM: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v:.4f}" for k, v in first_delay.items()))
        pre = t < C.GO
        mm_pt_b = ab[MM & (proj == 'PT') & keep][:, pre].mean(0).max()
        print(f"   (c) reference, maximum mean |beta| before the go cue: MM PT {mm_pt_b:.4f}, "
              f"MM IT {ab[MM & (proj == 'IT') & keep][:, pre].mean(0).max():.4f}, ALM PT {ab[ALM & (proj == 'PT') & keep][:, pre].mean(0).max():.4f} "
              f"(the criterion's ALM deep maximum needs depth; for MM PT to pass it must exceed {2 * mm_pt_b:.4f})")
pt_mm = MM & (proj == "PT")
print(f"\nMM PT ROIs with F0 <= 0 on some trial: {int((pt_mm & ~v2).sum())} of {int(pt_mm.sum())}")
print("MM PT ROIs by animal: " + ", ".join(
    f"{a} {int((pt_mm & (animal == a)).sum())} ROIs in {len(np.unique(plane[pt_mm & (animal == a)]))} planes, "
    f"{int((pt_mm & ~v2 & (animal == a)).sum())} of them with F0 <= 0 on some trial" for a in labelled_mice))

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient), not decided here. Under the paper's account that PT neurons are deep, part (a) holds for PT: the maximum of mean |alpha| from trial start to 2.2 s is 0.623 in MM PT against 0.033 in ALM PT (T1, V1; T2 0.586 against 0.033; V2 0.704 against 0.029), larger in 0.977 of the resamples that hold both groups (29 of 1,000 lack one). The MM PT mean is uncertain: its bootstrap SD (0.617) is as large as the mean, and 280 of the 334 MM PT ROIs are in 7 planes of one mouse (an064). Without the depth split, MM IT (0.057 against 0.027) and other ROIs (0.122 against 0.025) are also above ALM. The other groups of part (a), and parts (b) and (c), need depth, so the claim stays blocked. Part (c) looks unlikely to hold for PT on the same account: the maximum of mean |beta| before the go cue is 0.523 in MM PT (T1, V1), so the ALM deep maximum would have to exceed 1.047, against 0.112 in ALM PT. The large MM PT values may come from a few ROIs: 280 of the 334 MM PT ROIs, and 45 of the 47 with F0 <= 0 on some trial, are in an064.

fig8ef-area-explains-variance (blocked; area against projection type)¶

Coding is mainly determined by cortical location; cortical area (ALM against MM) and cell depth explain most of the variance of selectivity, more than projection type.

The criterion needs the depth grouping in both of its conditions, and the files hold no depth, so the claim is blocked. Area and projection type are in the files, and their total variance explained is computed here as the criterion defines it (SSB over SST, summed over the bins from 4.6 s before to 2.5 s after the go cue and over |alpha|, |beta| and |gamma|, non-significant set to 0), under readings N1 (three labelled mice for both groupings) and N2 (all six mice for area). It does not decide: if area explains less than projection type, area is not the largest and the claim is at best partially reproduced, depending on depth; if more, depth decides whether area is the largest.

In [29]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(86)
names3 = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]

def var_explained(idx, b, w, labels):
    X = A[b]["coef_sig"][idx][:, w]
    ssb = sst = 0.0
    per = {}
    for k in range(3):
        bk, tk = C.ss_between(np.abs(X[..., k]), labels)
        ssb, sst = ssb + bk.sum(), sst + tk.sum()
        per[f"|{names3[k]}|"] = bk.sum() / tk.sum()
        bs, ts = C.ss_between(X[..., k], labels)
        per[names3[k]] = bs.sum() / ts.sum()
    return ssb / sst, per

for b in ("T1", "T2"):
    t = A[b]["times"]; w = (t >= -0.4 - 1e-9) & (t <= 6.7 + 1e-9)
    for vname, keep in (("V1", np.ones(len(cells), bool)), ("V2, F0 > 0 on every trial", v2)):
        i1, iall = np.flatnonzero(lab_m & keep), np.flatnonzero(keep)
        res = {"area, N1": var_explained(i1, b, w, area[i1]), "projection type, N1": var_explained(i1, b, w, proj[i1]),
               "area, N2": var_explained(iall, b, w, area[iall])}
        print(f"{b} {vname} (bins {w.sum()}, ROIs N1 {len(i1)}, N2 {len(iall)}):")
        for k, (tot, per) in res.items():
            print(f"   {k}: total {tot:.4f}; per coefficient " + ", ".join(f"{c} {v:.4f}" for c, v in per.items()))
        print(f"   area above projection type (N1): {res['area, N1'][0] > res['projection type, N1'][0]}")
        if b == "T1":
            bt = []
            for _ in range(1000):
                ix = C.joint_resample(animal, plane, [lab_m & keep], rng)[0]
                bt.append((var_explained(ix, b, w, area[ix])[0], var_explained(ix, b, w, proj[ix])[0]))
            bt = np.array(bt)
            print(f"   hierarchical bootstrap (N1, 1000 resamples): SD area {bt[:, 0].std():.4f}, projection type "
                  f"{bt[:, 1].std():.4f}; resamples with area above projection type {np.mean(bt[:, 0] > bt[:, 1]):.3f}")

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient), not decided here. Projection type explains more of the variance of selectivity than area in every reading run: total 0.0013 against 0.0005 under N1 (T1, V1; area under N2 0.0007), and the same order with T2 and with V2. Both totals are small, and the hierarchical bootstrap does not separate them (SD 0.0019 for area and 0.0011 for projection type; area above projection type in 0.414 of resamples, 0.400 under V2). If this order holds, area is not the largest of the three groupings, so the claim cannot be reproduced; whether it is partially reproduced or not depends on depth (area and depth together against projection type), which is not in the files.

alm-pt-it-lick-fraction-below-20¶

Even in ALM, less than 20% of PT or IT cells displayed lick direction selectivity at any given time, and the onset timing was variable.

ephys-pt-it-onset-not-detected¶

The difference in onset of lick direction selectivity between PT and IT neurons was not detected in an electrophysiology dataset recorded under similar conditions (45 PT and 27 IT cells, Li et al., 2015).

The readings are those the criterion names since the question was answered: (1) spike counts in 400 ms windows in 100 ms steps, each window placed at its centre; (2) trials of the four types without photostimulation, early-lick trials excluded by the early_lick column, time from the sample event (pole movement onset); (3) onset by convention O from trial start to the go cue, rules S1 and S2, baselines O1 (windows wholly before trial start) and O2 (windows wholly within the 0.5 s before it); (4) units of all sessions pooled, bootstrap H2 over units and H1 hierarchical over animals, sessions and units. The 3-way ANOVA and the coefficients are those of convention M, applied to the counts of each unit. A trial is photostimulated when a laser pulse (from the laser power series) or a photostim_start_time event falls within it. Only the sessions with a tagged unit are read, and of each unit only the trials within its observation intervals.

In [32]:

           "O2": (li_centres - C.EPH_WIN / 2 >= -0.5 - 1e-9) & (li_centres + C.EPH_WIN / 2 <= 1e-9)}
print(f"window centres {li_centres[0]:.1f} to {li_centres[-1]:.1f} s; baseline windows (centres): "
      + "; ".join(f"{k} {list(li_centres[v])}" for k, v in li_base.items()))
LB, li_lab, li_animal, li_sess, li_ntr, dropped = [], [], [], [], [], []
for si, s in enumerate(S):

        cnt = {t: int((types == t).sum()) for t in C.TYPES}

    for _ in range(1000):
        ip, ii = C.joint_resample(li_animal, li_sess, [lpt, lit], rng, hier)
        bp, bi = LB[ip].mean(0), LB[ii].mean(0)
        for (o, r), lst in d.items():
            on = lambda c: C.onset(c, li_centres, rule=r, go=go_li, base=li_base[o], search_end=go_li)
            lst.append(on(bi) - on(bp))
    for (o, r), lst in d.items():
        on = lambda c: C.onset(c, li_centres, rule=r, go=go_li, base=li_base[o], search_end=go_li)
        dd = np.array(lst)
        rows.append({"baseline": o, "rule": r, "bootstrap": "H1" if hier else "H2", "PT_onset": on(cp), "IT_onset": on(ci),
                     "IT_minus_PT": on(ci) - on(cp), "boot_sd": np.nanstd(dd), "p_not_earlier": np.mean(~(dd > 0)),
                     "no_onset": int(np.isnan(dd).sum())})
lres = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["rule", "baseline", "bootstrap"])
lres["PT_earlier_p_below_0.01"] = lres.p_not_earlier < 0.01
print(lres.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nCombinations finding PT earlier at p < 0.01:", int(lres["PT_earlier_p_below_0.01"].sum()), "of", len(lres))
for o in ("O1", "O2"):
    for lab_, c in (("PT", cp), ("IT", ci)):
        bm = c[li_base[o]]
        print(f"{o} {lab_}: baseline mean {bm.mean():.4f}, SD {bm.std(ddof=1):.4f}, threshold {bm.mean() + 6 * bm.std(ddof=1):.4f}")
plt.figure(figsize=(5.5, 3))
plt.plot(li_centres, cp, label=f"PT (n={int(lpt.sum())})"); plt.plot(li_centres, ci, label=f"IT (n={int(lit.sum())})")
for x in (0, 1.3, go_li):
    plt.axvline(x, color="k", lw=0.5)
plt.xlabel("window centre, time from the sample event (s)"); plt.ylabel("mean |beta| (spikes per window)"); plt.legend(); plt.show()
print(f"plotted range PT {cp.min():.3f} to {cp.max():.3f}, IT {ci.min():.3f} to {ci.max():.3f}")
print("by animal (O1, S1), onset PT / IT: " + "; ".join(
    f"{a} {C.onset(LB[lpt & (li_animal == a)].mean(0), li_centres, base=li_base['O1'], search_end=go_li) if (lpt & (li_animal == a)).any() else np.nan:.1f} / "
    f"{C.onset(LB[lit & (li_animal == a)].mean(0), li_centres, base=li_base['O1'], search_end=go_li) if (lit & (li_animal == a)).any() else np.nan:.1f}"
    for a in np.unique(li_animal)))

Result: reproduced. No combination of readings finds the 45 PT units earlier than the 26 IT units at p < 0.01: the IT minus PT onset is 0.7 s with rule S1 (bootstrap SD 0.66 to 0.75 s, p 0.30 to 0.34) and 0.2 s with rule S2 (SD 0.63 to 0.64 s, p 0.15 to 0.20). Baselines O1 and O2 are the same two windows, as spikes are stored only from 0.52 s before the sample event, so the 8 combinations give 4 distinct results. Two overlapping windows give a weak baseline: the IT baseline SD is 0.0004 (threshold 0.0228 against a mean of 0.0205), and the PT onset under S1 (0.1 s) falls in the sample epoch, so the test carries little information. The onset difference is positive in every combination, smaller than in the imaging and not significant. One IT unit (mouse 219253) has no ER trial without photostimulation and cannot be fitted; 26 of the 27 IT units are analysed. 4,152 of 16,571 trials in these sessions had photostimulation and are left out.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The time bins (frames on one grid, or 66.7 ms by interpolation), dF/F with baselines F0 <= 0 kept (V1), the onset rules (S1, S2) and the bootstrap details are readings from the claims file's conventions, which the paper does not fix (five questions were answered, each with "the paper does not say"); several claims use thresholds the claims file fixed itself (2 bootstrap SD, more than half of bins). Area comes from the files' label. Readings that need depth or coordinates could not be run. The PT and IT onset difference matches the paper only under one onset rule (S2), only with T2 bins and only with the bootstrap over cells. The Li et al. (2015) units are analysed with the paper's 400 ms windows on trials without photostimulation; one IT unit cannot be fitted. fig8d-pt-contra-bias and fig8d-mm-posterior-preferring, and the bootstrap part of fig8d-error-outnumber-correct, find the stated direction at 1.56 to 1.94 bootstrap SDs, short of the 2 SD bound the claims file fixed. The per-bin selectivity fractions are low (ALM purely lick-direction selective at most 6.2% with T1 bins, 6.5% with T2), and the rules that count neurons selective in any bin count many chance bins: with permuted trial types figs5-single-coefficient's criterion is met in every bin and the groups of fig4a-lick-direction-epochs and fig4b-object-location-memory exist, so those outcomes rest on their criteria, not on a difference from chance. The peak of figs4-peak-shift is taken over the whole window; before the go cue MM peaks first.

What was found about the dataset. Each of the 105 planes is deposited twice, under different identifiers. ImagingPlane.location says ALM for every plane, also the MM ones. No text value in any file names a depth, a coordinate or a layer. The plane depth, the cells' coordinates, the imaging location within a mouse and the lick times are not in the files, nor are the wide-field imaging, the whisker tracking, the photoinhibition data and the silicon probe recordings; the CRCNS DOI the paper gives for its data is an unfilled placeholder, and a search of DANDI finds no other deposit. The included column marks 8,655 ROIs without saying why. After neuropil subtraction, 1,262 ROIs have a zero or negative baseline on some trial. Early-lick trials carry no pole position. The counts of planes, ROIs, areas, PT and IT cells and trials agree with the paper.
